exposure: mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. normal delivery)
cohort: 80 full-term, mature neonates of both sexes; 40 born via normal delivery and 40 delivered by elective cesarean section under regional (spinal) anesthesia
finding: Cesarean-delivered neonates had significantly higher methemoglobin levels and lower G6PD and GSH levels compared to neonates delivered vaginally.
mod_finding: Cesarean-delivered neonates had significantly higher levels of oxidative stress (higher methemoglobin, lower G6PD and GSH) compared to vaginally delivered neonates, but there was no significant difference in nitrosative stress (serum nitrate and nitrite) between the groups.
